newsitem.title: SYRIA: Iranian minister opens military talks in Syria.
newsitem.headline: Iranian minister opens military talks in Syria.

text.p: Iran's Defence Minister Mohammad Forouzandeh began talks on Saturday with Syrian leaders on ways to increase military cooperation between them, officials said.
They said Forouzandeh discussed the latest developments in the region with Prime Minister Mahmoud Zu'bi after talks with his Syrian counterpart Lieutenant-General Mustafa Tlas.
An Iranian official said Forouzandeh's visit was aimed at "promoting the strategic ties between the Islamic Republic of Iran and Syria."
Diplomats said the talks were covering the situation in south Lebanon where tension has recently increased between Israeli troops and fighters of the pro-Iranian Hizbollah (Party of God).
The diplomats noted the visit followed reports that Iran was sending missiles to Hizbollah fighters through Damascus.

Iran and Syria, which is a main foreign power broker in Lebanon where it has some 35,000 troops, back Hizbollah fighters in their war against Israeli troops who occupy a strip of south Lebanon to prevent guerrillas reaching Israel.
Syria has had close ties with Tehran since the Islamic revolution in 1979 and backed Iran in its war with Iraq between 1980 and 1988.
Both also back militant Palestinian groups, including Hamas and the Islamic Jihad who claimed several suicide attacks in Israel that killed scores of people.
